01Rationale

Why this level matters

AI now drafts plans, tracks risks and summarises status. A good manager still sets the goal, owns the trade-offs and keeps the team moving. This course covers the core methods, and how to use AI without losing control of the work.

02Target competencies

Intended learning outcomes

Plan the work

Write a clear charter, scope, schedule and risk list.

Run delivery

Run Agile and Scrum teams, and report status that people trust.

Improve operations

Map processes and find the bottleneck in operations and supply chains.

Use AI well

Use AI for plans and reports while checking and owning the result.

Module 1Project foundations

Module 2Agile delivery

Module 3Operations

  2. Checking AI plans and reports
  3. Preparing for project management certifications
  4. Your project portfolio

04Planned practical work

A project, planned and run

Proposed project: Plan and run a small project from charter to review, using AI for drafts and checking each one. This practical component will be developed and validated before the level opens.

The steps

  1. Write the charter
  2. Build the plan and schedule
  3. Write the risk register
  4. Run two sprints on a board
  5. Build the status report
  6. Hold the review and write what you learned

Intended validation criteria

  • Every task has an owner and a date
  • Every risk has a response
  • You checked each AI-written plan and report

05How you learn

Proposed learning design

Worked examples

The professional academies begin with complete examples and make the reasoning behind good decisions visible.

Guided practice

Scaffolds fade as learners progress—from annotated examples to structured tasks and independent work.

Retrieval and review

Low-stakes questions prompt recall; review revisits important concepts. Model answers and rubrics make improvement specific.

Research-informed updates

The academies cite primary research and standards, record review dates and receive versioned updates as evidence changes.

The proposed learning design draws on retrieval practice, worked examples and spaced review; detailed learner materials will be published before release. Read the evidence and sources.

06Intended audience

What you need

No experience needed. Some experience working in a team helps.
